## Appendix: What about fish?
##### Available estimates for the number of fish killed
Overall, it seems clear that at least hundreds of millions of fish are killed every day, but as emphasized throughout this article, the uncertainty is very large. Understanding how many animals are killed by humans and closing these gaps in our statistical understanding of the world would be important.

## Appendix: What about fish?
### Endnotes
1.   A body length of 2m is a conservative estimate. The typical Holstein Friesian has a body length between 2.35m and 2.5m.
The distance between Madrid and Amsterdam is about 1800 kilometers.
Yearly, this is more than 16 times the circumference of Earth (40,075 km): 365*1800km=657,000km and 657,000km/40,075 km=16.4
2.   The data that this chart is based on can be explored in this interactive chart on the yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. The interactive chart also allows you to explore this data for countries around the world and over time.
These numbers only represent the number of animals slaughtered for meat. This means, for example, that these numbers do not include the number of male chicks that are killed in the egg industry (see chick culling on Wikipedia).
The chart is based on the data for 2021, which is the latest available data at the time of writing in July ‘23.
The calculations for the numbers shown in the chart are as follows:
**Cattle:** 331,950,000 cows per year
→ 331,950,000/365.25 = **908,830 per day**
**Goats:** 500,870,000 per year
→ 500,870,000/365.25 = **1,371,307 per day**
**Sheep:** 617,260,000 per year
→ 617,260,000/365.25 = **1,689,966 per day**
**Pigs:** 1,400,000,000 per year
→ 1,400,000,000/365.25 = **3,832,991 per day**

## Appendix: What about fish?
### Endnotes
**Ducks:**4,310,000,000 per year
**→**4,310,000,000/365.25=**11,800,137 per day**
**Chicken:**73,790,000,000 per year
→ 73,790,000,000/365.25 = **202,026,010 per day**
→ 202,026,010/(24*60) = 140,296 per minute
All data here comes from the UN’s Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO). While this is the best, most comprehensive data available, it is far from perfect, and the uncertainties around the estimates are considerable. A discussion (from 2019) of some of the issues of animal counts in the FAO data can be found in this article by Saulius Šimčikas at Rethink Priorities: Accuracy issues in FAO animal numbers.
3.   We’ve written extensively about this problem here on Our World in Data. Articles that discuss the evidence and the scale of this issue include:

4.   Not just land animals would benefit: Livestock farming is also a significant source of phosphorus and nitrogen runoffs from the use of animal manure as fertilizer. Less of these nutrient runoffs would mean fewer instances of harmful algal blooms in bodies of water, thereby improving water quality and preserving aquatic biodiversity.

Title: Our World in Data on Instagram: "How many animals get slaughtered for meat every day?

On Our World in Data, we cover many topics related to reducing human suffering: alleviating poverty, reducing child and maternal mortality, curing diseases, and ending hunger.

But if we aim to reduce *total* suffering, society’s ability to reduce this in other animals — which feel pain, too — also matters.

This is especially true when we look at the numbers: every year, humans slaughter more than 80 *billion* land-based animals for farming alone. Most of these animals are raised in factory farms, often in painful and inhumane conditions.

Estimates for fish are more uncertain, but when we include them, these numbers more than double.

These numbers are large — but this also means that there are large opportunities to alleviate animal suffering by reducing the number of animals we use for food, science, cosmetics, and other industries, and improving the living conditions of those we continue to raise.

🔗 Click the link in bio to explore our new page on animal welfare, where you can find all of our data, visualizations, and writing on the topic, including four new articles.

Data source: @fao

How many animals get slaughtered for meat every day?
On Our World in Data, we cover many topics related to reducing human suffering: alleviating poverty, reducing child and maternal mortality, curing diseases, and ending hunger.
But if we aim to reduce *total* suffering, society’s ability to reduce this in other animals — which feel pain, too — also matters.
This is especially true when we look at the numbers: every year, humans slaughter more than 80 *billion* land-based animals for farming alone. Most of these animals are raised in factory farms, often in painful and inhumane conditions.
Estimates for fish are more uncertain, but when we include them, these numbers more than double.
These numbers are large — but this also means that there are large opportunities to alleviate animal suffering by reducing the number of animals we use for food, science, cosmetics, and other industries, and improving the living conditions of those we continue to raise.

Estimates for fish are more uncertain, but when we include them, these numbers more than double.
These numbers are large — but this also means that there are large opportunities to alleviate animal suffering by reducing the number of animals we use for food, science, cosmetics, and other industries, and improving the living conditions of those we continue to raise.

opened.anchor: How many animals are slaughtered every day worldwide?
opened.information:
Source: https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/
Title: How many animals are slaughtered every day worldwide?
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
Animal welfare

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
Every day, more than 230 million land animals are slaughtered for meat worldwide. Nine in ten are chickens.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026. The figure comes from the FAO, the United Nations food and agriculture agency. Yet it leaves out most of the animals killed: fish. Nobody counts them one by one, but a study published in 2024 estimates that fishing catches between 3 and 6 billion of them a day.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6. This article traces each figure back to its source, then looks at what a donation can change.
In brief
*   In 2024, **86 billion** land animals were slaughtered for meat worldwide, roughly **2,700 a second**.  
*   Farmed fish are killed in the **hundreds of billions** each year, and wild fish in the **trillions**.  
*   In France, around **2.6 million** land animals are sent to slaughter every day.  
*   Your donations can prevent a great deal of animal suffering: by our estimates, **€0.85** spares one hen a life in a cage, on average.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Per day, per year, per second
Every year, the FAO publishes the number of animals slaughtered for meat in each country. Our World in Data compiles these figures and makes them available to download. In 2024, the most recent year available, the total reached 86.3 billion animals across seven species: chickens, ducks, pigs, sheep, goats, turkeys and cattle.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026.
That works out at 236 million animals a day, or 2,700 a second.
This total is a minimum: rabbits, geese, guinea fowl and horses are not included.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Species by species
Chickens Other species
Land animals slaughtered per day worldwide in 2024. Linear scale: next to the chickens, the bars for the other species are barely visible. Source: FAO, via Our World in Data.
| Species | Slaughtered in 2024 | Per day (approx.) | Share of total |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Chickens | 78.5 billion | 215 million | 91% |  
| Ducks | 4.2 billion | 11.6 million | 4.9% |  
| Pigs | 1.5 billion | 4.1 million | 1.7% |  
| Sheep | 704 million | 1.9 million | 0.8% |  
| Goats | 564 million | 1.5 million | 0.7% |  
| Turkeys | 504 million | 1.4 million | 0.6% |  
| Cattle | 305 million | 830,000 | 0.4% |  
| Total | 86.3 billion | 236 million | 100% |
Source: FAO, via Our World in Data. Per day: annual total divided by 365.25.
Worldwide, around 257 chickens are slaughtered for every head of cattle.
The lives of these animals can change. A single campaign aimed at companies can affect millions of them: in 2023, The Humane League pressed 62 companies to honour their own commitments, which cover 42 million hens. We come back to this at the end of the article.

## Why chickens make up 9 in 10 of the animals slaughtered
Weight explains much of the gap. In France, a broiler chicken yields 1.6 kg of meat on average (carcass weight), compared with 323 kg for one head of cattle.[[3]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn3)Agreste (2025). Statistique agricole annuelle 2024, résultats définitifs (French annual agricultural statistics). Chiffres et données no. 16, pp. 2... It therefore takes around 200 chickens to produce as much meat as a single cow or bull.
Slaughter age matters too. In the European Union, a fast-growing chicken goes to slaughter at around 37 days old, weighing 2 to 2.5 kg, before it has even reached sexual maturity. According to EFSA, the European Food Safety Authority, this is the result of genetic selection: between 1950 and 2000, the growth rate of these chickens quadrupled.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126. Slower-growing breeds, such as Label Rouge chickens, must reach at least 70 to 81 days before slaughter.
This intensive model supplies 90% of broiler chickens in the European Union. The animals bear the cost: EFSA reports walking problems of genetic origin in these birds, which breeders have reduced but never eliminated.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126.

## What about fish?
The FAO counts fish in tonnes, never as individuals.[[5]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn5)Roser, M. (2023). How many animals get slaughtered every day? Our World in Data. To work out how many there are, you have to divide the tonnage by an average weight for each species. Alison Mood and Phil Brooke (fishcount) did exactly that in two studies published in the scientific journal _Animal Welfare_.
236 m land animals slaughtered per day (2024)
340 m farmed fish killed per day (central estimate, 2019)
3 to 6 bn wild fish caught per day (2000-2019 average)

## What about fish?
### Farmed fish
In 2019, between 78 and 171 billion farmed fish were killed for food. The central estimate is 124 billion, or around 340 million a day. According to the authors, farmed fish now outnumber all the farmed birds and mammals slaughtered. Their number has risen ninefold since 1990.[[6]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn6)Mood, A., Lara, E., Boyland, N. K. and Brooke, P. (2023). Estimating global numbers of farmed fishes killed for food annually from 1990 to 2019. An...

## What about fish?
### Wild fish
Fishing kills even more. Between 2000 and 2019, an average of 1.1 to 2.2 trillion wild fish were caught each year, or 3 to 6 billion a day. According to the authors, more than half of them are turned into fishmeal and fish oil.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6.

Title: How many animals are slaughtered every day worldwide?
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
Animal welfare

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
Every day, more than 230 million land animals are slaughtered for meat worldwide. Nine in ten are chickens.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026. The figure comes from the FAO, the United Nations food and agriculture agency. Yet it leaves out most of the animals killed: fish. Nobody counts them one by one, but a study published in 2024 estimates that fishing catches between 3 and 6 billion of them a day.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6. This article traces each figure back to its source, then looks at what a donation can change.
In brief
*   In 2024, **86 billion** land animals were slaughtered for meat worldwide, roughly **2,700 a second**.  
*   Farmed fish are killed in the **hundreds of billions** each year, and wild fish in the **trillions**.  
*   In France, around **2.6 million** land animals are sent to slaughter every day.  
*   Your donations can prevent a great deal of animal suffering: by our estimates, **€0.85** spares one hen a life in a cage, on average.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Per day, per year, per second
Every year, the FAO publishes the number of animals slaughtered for meat in each country. Our World in Data compiles these figures and makes them available to download. In 2024, the most recent year available, the total reached 86.3 billion animals across seven species: chickens, ducks, pigs, sheep, goats, turkeys and cattle.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026.
That works out at 236 million animals a day, or 2,700 a second.
This total is a minimum: rabbits, geese, guinea fowl and horses are not included.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Species by species
Chickens Other species
Land animals slaughtered per day worldwide in 2024. Linear scale: next to the chickens, the bars for the other species are barely visible. Source: FAO, via Our World in Data.
| Species | Slaughtered in 2024 | Per day (approx.) | Share of total |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Chickens | 78.5 billion | 215 million | 91% |  
| Ducks | 4.2 billion | 11.6 million | 4.9% |  
| Pigs | 1.5 billion | 4.1 million | 1.7% |  
| Sheep | 704 million | 1.9 million | 0.8% |  
| Goats | 564 million | 1.5 million | 0.7% |  
| Turkeys | 504 million | 1.4 million | 0.6% |  
| Cattle | 305 million | 830,000 | 0.4% |  
| Total | 86.3 billion | 236 million | 100% |
Source: FAO, via Our World in Data. Per day: annual total divided by 365.25.
Worldwide, around 257 chickens are slaughtered for every head of cattle.
The lives of these animals can change. A single campaign aimed at companies can affect millions of them: in 2023, The Humane League pressed 62 companies to honour their own commitments, which cover 42 million hens. We come back to this at the end of the article.

## Why chickens make up 9 in 10 of the animals slaughtered
Weight explains much of the gap. In France, a broiler chicken yields 1.6 kg of meat on average (carcass weight), compared with 323 kg for one head of cattle.[[3]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn3)Agreste (2025). Statistique agricole annuelle 2024, résultats définitifs (French annual agricultural statistics). Chiffres et données no. 16, pp. 2... It therefore takes around 200 chickens to produce as much meat as a single cow or bull.
Slaughter age matters too. In the European Union, a fast-growing chicken goes to slaughter at around 37 days old, weighing 2 to 2.5 kg, before it has even reached sexual maturity. According to EFSA, the European Food Safety Authority, this is the result of genetic selection: between 1950 and 2000, the growth rate of these chickens quadrupled.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126. Slower-growing breeds, such as Label Rouge chickens, must reach at least 70 to 81 days before slaughter.
This intensive model supplies 90% of broiler chickens in the European Union. The animals bear the cost: EFSA reports walking problems of genetic origin in these birds, which breeders have reduced but never eliminated.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126.

## What about fish?
The FAO counts fish in tonnes, never as individuals.[[5]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn5)Roser, M. (2023). How many animals get slaughtered every day? Our World in Data. To work out how many there are, you have to divide the tonnage by an average weight for each species. Alison Mood and Phil Brooke (fishcount) did exactly that in two studies published in the scientific journal _Animal Welfare_.
236 m land animals slaughtered per day (2024)
340 m farmed fish killed per day (central estimate, 2019)
3 to 6 bn wild fish caught per day (2000-2019 average)

## What about fish?
### Farmed fish
In 2019, between 78 and 171 billion farmed fish were killed for food. The central estimate is 124 billion, or around 340 million a day. According to the authors, farmed fish now outnumber all the farmed birds and mammals slaughtered. Their number has risen ninefold since 1990.[[6]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn6)Mood, A., Lara, E., Boyland, N. K. and Brooke, P. (2023). Estimating global numbers of farmed fishes killed for food annually from 1990 to 2019. An...

## What about fish?
### Wild fish
Fishing kills even more. Between 2000 and 2019, an average of 1.1 to 2.2 trillion wild fish were caught each year, or 3 to 6 billion a day. According to the authors, more than half of them are turned into fishmeal and fish oil.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6.

We need to get specific data: 5 countries with biggest decrease in yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat between 2000 and 2007 in cattle category (according to Our World in Data). Then find the country among those 5 with the lowest total production tons during 2000-2007 (production tons? maybe "total production tons" refers to FAO aquaculture production data? Actually we need country with lowest amount of total production tons during the timeframe 2000-2007, according to FAO Aquaculture Production data? Wait: "in the country with the lowest amount of total production tons during the previously mentioned timeframe (2000-2007), according to FishBase.org's FAO Aquaculture Production data". So we need to compare FAO Aquaculture Production data (tangible tons) for each of those countries across 2000-2007, sum total production tons, find lowest. Then for that country, we look at FishBase.org's FAO Aquaculture Production data. But what species? "what are the scientific name of the species that are marked as having produced more than 0 tons in 2001 in the country... according to FishBase.org's FAO Aquaculture Production data?" So we need to look at the FishBase data for that country, for year 2001, species with >0 tons. Provide scientific names.

Thus steps:

1. Get Our World in Data dataset for cattle slaughtered numbers per country per year 2000-2007.

2. For each country, compute decrease (2000 minus 2007?) maybe difference 2000 - 2007. Find 5 countries with largest drop (biggest decrease).

3. Identify those 5 countries.

4. For each of those countries, get FAO Aquaculture Production data from FishBase (year 2000-2007). Sum total production tons across species per year? Total production tons maybe sum over all species. Find which country has lowest total production across period. That is the country of interest.

5. For that country, get species list for year 2001 with produced >0 tons. Provide scientific names.

We need data sources.

Our World in Data provides a grapher for "cattle slaughtered". Might need to download CSV.

Similarly FishBase's FAO aquaculture production data can be accessed as a dataset (maybe "FAO Aquaculture Production and Trade Data 1970-2000") but FishBase provides a dataset "FAO Aquaculture Production" with columns: Country, Year, Species, Production (tons). We need to find year 2001, species >0.

We must get data programmatically or search for information.

Could use the OWID grapher API: https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/animals-slaughtered-for-meat?download-format=csv&download=some but we need cattle only. The API: https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/animals-slaughtered-for-meat?download-format=csv&download-csv because grapher components offer download? Alternatively we could use more specific endpoint for cattle (cattle?). Might be there is a dataset for cattle data: "cattle" variable? Search: "cattle slaughtered ourworldindata".

Title: How many animals are slaughtered every day worldwide?
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
Animal welfare

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
Every day, more than 230 million land animals are slaughtered for meat worldwide. Nine in ten are chickens.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026. The figure comes from the FAO, the United Nations food and agriculture agency. Yet it leaves out most of the animals killed: fish. Nobody counts them one by one, but a study published in 2024 estimates that fishing catches between 3 and 6 billion of them a day.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6. This article traces each figure back to its source, then looks at what a donation can change.
In brief
*   In 2024, **86 billion** land animals were slaughtered for meat worldwide, roughly **2,700 a second**.  
*   Farmed fish are killed in the **hundreds of billions** each year, and wild fish in the **trillions**.  
*   In France, around **2.6 million** land animals are sent to slaughter every day.  
*   Your donations can prevent a great deal of animal suffering: by our estimates, **€0.85** spares one hen a life in a cage, on average.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Per day, per year, per second
Every year, the FAO publishes the number of animals slaughtered for meat in each country. Our World in Data compiles these figures and makes them available to download. In 2024, the most recent year available, the total reached 86.3 billion animals across seven species: chickens, ducks, pigs, sheep, goats, turkeys and cattle.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026.
That works out at 236 million animals a day, or 2,700 a second.
This total is a minimum: rabbits, geese, guinea fowl and horses are not included.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Species by species
Chickens Other species
Land animals slaughtered per day worldwide in 2024. Linear scale: next to the chickens, the bars for the other species are barely visible. Source: FAO, via Our World in Data.
| Species | Slaughtered in 2024 | Per day (approx.) | Share of total |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Chickens | 78.5 billion | 215 million | 91% |  
| Ducks | 4.2 billion | 11.6 million | 4.9% |  
| Pigs | 1.5 billion | 4.1 million | 1.7% |  
| Sheep | 704 million | 1.9 million | 0.8% |  
| Goats | 564 million | 1.5 million | 0.7% |  
| Turkeys | 504 million | 1.4 million | 0.6% |  
| Cattle | 305 million | 830,000 | 0.4% |  
| Total | 86.3 billion | 236 million | 100% |
Source: FAO, via Our World in Data. Per day: annual total divided by 365.25.
Worldwide, around 257 chickens are slaughtered for every head of cattle.
The lives of these animals can change. A single campaign aimed at companies can affect millions of them: in 2023, The Humane League pressed 62 companies to honour their own commitments, which cover 42 million hens. We come back to this at the end of the article.

## Why chickens make up 9 in 10 of the animals slaughtered
Weight explains much of the gap. In France, a broiler chicken yields 1.6 kg of meat on average (carcass weight), compared with 323 kg for one head of cattle.[[3]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn3)Agreste (2025). Statistique agricole annuelle 2024, résultats définitifs (French annual agricultural statistics). Chiffres et données no. 16, pp. 2... It therefore takes around 200 chickens to produce as much meat as a single cow or bull.
Slaughter age matters too. In the European Union, a fast-growing chicken goes to slaughter at around 37 days old, weighing 2 to 2.5 kg, before it has even reached sexual maturity. According to EFSA, the European Food Safety Authority, this is the result of genetic selection: between 1950 and 2000, the growth rate of these chickens quadrupled.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126. Slower-growing breeds, such as Label Rouge chickens, must reach at least 70 to 81 days before slaughter.
This intensive model supplies 90% of broiler chickens in the European Union. The animals bear the cost: EFSA reports walking problems of genetic origin in these birds, which breeders have reduced but never eliminated.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126.

## What about fish?
The FAO counts fish in tonnes, never as individuals.[[5]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn5)Roser, M. (2023). How many animals get slaughtered every day? Our World in Data. To work out how many there are, you have to divide the tonnage by an average weight for each species. Alison Mood and Phil Brooke (fishcount) did exactly that in two studies published in the scientific journal _Animal Welfare_.
236 m land animals slaughtered per day (2024)
340 m farmed fish killed per day (central estimate, 2019)
3 to 6 bn wild fish caught per day (2000-2019 average)

## What about fish?
### Farmed fish
In 2019, between 78 and 171 billion farmed fish were killed for food. The central estimate is 124 billion, or around 340 million a day. According to the authors, farmed fish now outnumber all the farmed birds and mammals slaughtered. Their number has risen ninefold since 1990.[[6]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn6)Mood, A., Lara, E., Boyland, N. K. and Brooke, P. (2023). Estimating global numbers of farmed fishes killed for food annually from 1990 to 2019. An...

## What about fish?
### Wild fish
Fishing kills even more. Between 2000 and 2019, an average of 1.1 to 2.2 trillion wild fish were caught each year, or 3 to 6 billion a day. According to the authors, more than half of them are turned into fishmeal and fish oil.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6.

Source: https://www.theworldcounts.com/footprint/food/cattle-slaughtered
Title: How many cows are killed each year?
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
FootprintFood & AgricultureCattle slaughtered for meat
Food & Agriculture
264,069,222
Cattle slaughtered for meat
cattle·Globally, this year

## About 305 million cattle a year
The world slaughtered about 305 million cattle for meat in 2024, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)1. That is roughly 10 cattle every second, or around 835,000 a day.
Next to the tens of billions of chickens slaughtered each year, that looks like a small number. Cattle are fewer than one in every 250 land animals killed for meat1. But each animal is enormous: a single cow or bull gives around 364 kilograms of meat, as much as about 210 chickens3. Together, beef and buffalo make up about a fifth of all the meat the world produces4.
The count covers cattle raised for beef and dairy cows slaughtered once they stop producing enough milk. It has grown slowly, from 173 million in 1961, and by only about 0.6% a year over the last decade1. At any time, around 1.58 billion cattle are alive on the world’s farms and ranches2.

## China, Brazil and the United States
China slaughtered the most cattle in 2024, 45.9 million, followed closely by Brazil with 39.7 million and the United States with 32.2 million. Together they account for more than a third of the world total. Argentina (13.9 million), Pakistan (10.5 million), Mexico (8.9 million) and Australia (8.7 million) follow1.
Brazil stands out. With about 212 million people, it has less than a sixth of China’s population10, but slaughters nearly as many cattle, and its cattle industry is tied to the fate of the Amazon rainforest, as the section below explains.

## Few animals, a huge footprint
Cattle are the most climate-heavy animals we eat. FAO estimates that livestock farming causes around 6.2 billion tonnes of greenhouse gases a year, and cattle, raised for meat and milk, account for about 3.8 billion tonnes of that, 62% of the total5.
62% of livestock emissions
That's the share of the livestock sector's greenhouse gases that comes from cattle, raised for meat and milk
The reason lies in how cattle digest their food. Cows are ruminants, animals with a multi-chamber stomach that ferments grass, and that process releases methane, a powerful greenhouse gas. Methane makes up slightly more than half of all livestock emissions5. Cattle also grow slowly, so each animal eats and emits for a long time before it is slaughtered.
Per kilogram, the gap is enormous. A kilogram of beef from a beef herd comes with around 99 kilograms of greenhouse gases, against about 10 for chicken6. Beef also needs about 15,400 cubic metres of water per tonne on average worldwide, mostly to grow the grass and feed, more than three times as much as chicken7.

## Pasture is the biggest driver of tropical deforestation
Cattle need space, and a lot of it comes from cleared forest. Between 2005 and 2013, the expansion of pasture for beef was responsible for 41% of all tropical deforestation, about 2.1 million hectares a year, more than any other single product. Beef production in Brazil alone accounted for about a quarter of all tropical forest lost8.
In the Amazon, the pattern is familiar: forest is cleared and turned into cattle pasture. Soy, palm oil and other crops play their part too, but beef is the largest single driver8.
The forests being cut down or burned, much of it for cattle pasture.

## Where beef is heading
Beef is growing more slowly than other meats. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and FAO expect beef consumption to rise by about 13% by 2034, while poultry grows by about 21%9. As a result, the livestock sector’s emissions are projected to rise by only about 6%, half as fast as meat production, because a growing share of the world’s meat comes from chicken rather than beef9.
That is good news for the climate, and bad news for the animal count: replacing the meat from one cow takes about 210 chickens, which is why the number of animals slaughtered keeps climbing much faster than the number of cattle. The full story is on the page for chickens slaughtered for meat.
The biggest question for cattle may be the Amazon. If Brazil manages to protect its forests while its cattle industry grows, it will show that beef and forests can coexist. If pasture keeps pushing into the rainforest, the true cost of a burger will keep including a piece of the world’s largest tropical forest. Which way it goes will depend far more on laws and their enforcement than on how much beef any one person eats.
Every land animal slaughtered for meat this year, cattle included.
Last updated 23 September 2026
How this number was made▾
This is the number of cattle FAO recorded as slaughtered for meat in 2024, the latest year published, spread evenly across the current year, so it runs at the 2024 pace. It includes dairy cows slaughtered at the end of their milking lives as well as cattle raised for beef. Buffalo are counted separately. The number grew only about 0.6% a year over the last decade, so we do not project it forward.
*    304,744,672 cattle slaughtered per year
FAO's measured 2024 total. Not extrapolated, since the series grows only about 0.6% a year and a projection would change the figure by little more than rounding.

## About 305 million cattle a year
The world slaughtered about 305 million cattle for meat in 2024, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)1. That is roughly 10 cattle every second, or around 835,000 a day.
Next to the tens of billions of chickens slaughtered each year, that looks like a small number. Cattle are fewer than one in every 250 land animals killed for meat1. But each animal is enormous: a single cow or bull gives around 364 kilograms of meat, as much as about 210 chickens3. Together, beef and buffalo make up about a fifth of all the meat the world produces4.
The count covers cattle raised for beef and dairy cows slaughtered once they stop producing enough milk. It has grown slowly, from 173 million in 1961, and by only about 0.6% a year over the last decade1. At any time, around 1.58 billion cattle are alive on the world’s farms and ranches2.
texts.2:
## China, Brazil and the United States
China slaughtered the most cattle in 2024, 45.9 million, followed closely by Brazil with 39.7 million and the United States with 32.2 million. Together they account for more than a third of the world total. Argentina (13.9 million), Pakistan (10.5 million), Mexico (8.9 million) and Australia (8.7 million) follow1.
Brazil stands out. With about 212 million people, it has less than a sixth of China’s population10, but slaughters nearly as many cattle, and its cattle industry is tied to the fate of the Amazon rainforest, as the section below explains.
texts.3:
## Few animals, a huge footprint
Cattle are the most climate-heavy animals we eat. FAO estimates that livestock farming causes around 6.2 billion tonnes of greenhouse gases a year, and cattle, raised for meat and milk, account for about 3.8 billion tonnes of that, 62% of the total5.
62% of livestock emissions
That's the share of the livestock sector's greenhouse gases that comes from cattle, raised for meat and milk
The reason lies in how cattle digest their food. Cows are ruminants, animals with a multi-chamber stomach that ferments grass, and that process releases methane, a powerful greenhouse gas. Methane makes up slightly more than half of all livestock emissions5. Cattle also grow slowly, so each animal eats and emits for a long time before it is slaughtered.
Per kilogram, the gap is enormous. A kilogram of beef from a beef herd comes with around 99 kilograms of greenhouse gases, against about 10 for chicken6. Beef also needs about 15,400 cubic metres of water per tonne on average worldwide, mostly to grow the grass and feed, more than three times as much as chicken7.
texts.4:
## Pasture is the biggest driver of tropical deforestation
Cattle need space, and a lot of it comes from cleared forest. Between 2005 and 2013, the expansion of pasture for beef was responsible for 41% of all tropical deforestation, about 2.1 million hectares a year, more than any other single product. Beef production in Brazil alone accounted for about a quarter of all tropical forest lost8.
In the Amazon, the pattern is familiar: forest is cleared and turned into cattle pasture. Soy, palm oil and other crops play their part too, but beef is the largest single driver8.
The forests being cut down or burned, much of it for cattle pasture.
texts.5:
## Where beef is heading
Beef is growing more slowly than other meats. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and FAO expect beef consumption to rise by about 13% by 2034, while poultry grows by about 21%9. As a result, the livestock sector’s emissions are projected to rise by only about 6%, half as fast as meat production, because a growing share of the world’s meat comes from chicken rather than beef9.
That is good news for the climate, and bad news for the animal count: replacing the meat from one cow takes about 210 chickens, which is why the number of animals slaughtered keeps climbing much faster than the number of cattle. The full story is on the page for chickens slaughtered for meat.
The biggest question for cattle may be the Amazon. If Brazil manages to protect its forests while its cattle industry grows, it will show that beef and forests can coexist. If pasture keeps pushing into the rainforest, the true cost of a burger will keep including a piece of the world’s largest tropical forest. Which way it goes will depend far more on laws and their enforcement than on how much beef any one person eats.
Every land animal slaughtered for meat this year, cattle included.
Last updated 23 September 2026
How this number was made▾
This is the number of cattle FAO recorded as slaughtered for meat in 2024, the latest year published, spread evenly across the current year, so it runs at the 2024 pace. It includes dairy cows slaughtered at the end of their milking lives as well as cattle raised for beef. Buffalo are counted separately. The number grew only about 0.6% a year over the last decade, so we do not project it forward.
*    304,744,672 cattle slaughtered per year
FAO's measured 2024 total. Not extrapolated, since the series grows only about 0.6% a year and a projection would change the figure by little more than rounding.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
Every day, more than 230 million land animals are slaughtered for meat worldwide. Nine in ten are chickens.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026. The figure comes from the FAO, the United Nations food and agriculture agency. Yet it leaves out most of the animals killed: fish. Nobody counts them one by one, but a study published in 2024 estimates that fishing catches between 3 and 6 billion of them a day.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6. This article traces each figure back to its source, then looks at what a donation can change.
In brief
*   In 2024, **86 billion** land animals were slaughtered for meat worldwide, roughly **2,700 a second**.  
*   Farmed fish are killed in the **hundreds of billions** each year, and wild fish in the **trillions**.  
*   In France, around **2.6 million** land animals are sent to slaughter every day.  
*   Your donations can prevent a great deal of animal suffering: by our estimates, **€0.85** spares one hen a life in a cage, on average.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Per day, per year, per second
Every year, the FAO publishes the number of animals slaughtered for meat in each country. Our World in Data compiles these figures and makes them available to download. In 2024, the most recent year available, the total reached 86.3 billion animals across seven species: chickens, ducks, pigs, sheep, goats, turkeys and cattle.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026.
That works out at 236 million animals a day, or 2,700 a second.
This total is a minimum: rabbits, geese, guinea fowl and horses are not included.

### Species by species

Worldwide, around 257 chickens are slaughtered for every head of cattle.
The lives of these animals can change. A single campaign aimed at companies can affect millions of them: in 2023, The Humane League pressed 62 companies to honour their own commitments, which cover 42 million hens. We come back to this at the end of the article.

## Why chickens make up 9 in 10 of the animals slaughtered
Weight explains much of the gap. In France, a broiler chicken yields 1.6 kg of meat on average (carcass weight), compared with 323 kg for one head of cattle.[[3]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn3)Agreste (2025). Statistique agricole annuelle 2024, résultats définitifs (French annual agricultural statistics). Chiffres et données no. 16, pp. 2... It therefore takes around 200 chickens to produce as much meat as a single cow or bull.
Slaughter age matters too. In the European Union, a fast-growing chicken goes to slaughter at around 37 days old, weighing 2 to 2.5 kg, before it has even reached sexual maturity. According to EFSA, the European Food Safety Authority, this is the result of genetic selection: between 1950 and 2000, the growth rate of these chickens quadrupled.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126. Slower-growing breeds, such as Label Rouge chickens, must reach at least 70 to 81 days before slaughter.
This intensive model supplies 90% of broiler chickens in the European Union. The animals bear the cost: EFSA reports walking problems of genetic origin in these birds, which breeders have reduced but never eliminated.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126.

## What about fish?
The FAO counts fish in tonnes, never as individuals.[[5]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn5)Roser, M. (2023). How many animals get slaughtered every day? Our World in Data. To work out how many there are, you have to divide the tonnage by an average weight for each species. Alison Mood and Phil Brooke (fishcount) did exactly that in two studies published in the scientific journal _Animal Welfare_.

In 2019, between 78 and 171 billion farmed fish were killed for food. The central estimate is 124 billion, or around 340 million a day. Fishing kills even more. Between 2000 and 2019, an average of 1.1 to 2.2 trillion wild fish were caught each year, or 3 to 6 billion a day. Title: How many cows are killed each year?
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
FootprintFood & AgricultureCattle slaughtered for meat
Food & Agriculture
264,069,222
Cattle slaughtered for meat
cattle·Globally, this year

## About 305 million cattle a year
The world slaughtered about 305 million cattle for meat in 2024, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)1. That is roughly 10 cattle every second, or around 835,000 a day.
Next to the tens of billions of chickens slaughtered each year, that looks like a small number. Cattle are fewer than one in every 250 land animals killed for meat1. But each animal is enormous: a single cow or bull gives around 364 kilograms of meat, as much as about 210 chickens3. Together, beef and buffalo make up about a fifth of all the meat the world produces4.
The count covers cattle raised for beef and dairy cows slaughtered once they stop producing enough milk. It has grown slowly, from 173 million in 1961, and by only about 0.6% a year over the last decade1. At any time, around 1.58 billion cattle are alive on the world’s farms and ranches2.

## China, Brazil and the United States
China slaughtered the most cattle in 2024, 45.9 million, followed closely by Brazil with 39.7 million and the United States with 32.2 million. Together they account for more than a third of the world total. Argentina (13.9 million), Pakistan (10.5 million), Mexico (8.9 million) and Australia (8.7 million) follow1.
Brazil stands out. With about 212 million people, it has less than a sixth of China’s population10, but slaughters nearly as many cattle, and its cattle industry is tied to the fate of the Amazon rainforest, as the section below explains.

## Few animals, a huge footprint
Cattle are the most climate-heavy animals we eat. FAO estimates that livestock farming causes around 6.2 billion tonnes of greenhouse gases a year, and cattle, raised for meat and milk, account for about 3.8 billion tonnes of that, 62% of the total5.
62% of livestock emissions
That's the share of the livestock sector's greenhouse gases that comes from cattle, raised for meat and milk
The reason lies in how cattle digest their food. Cows are ruminants, animals with a multi-chamber stomach that ferments grass, and that process releases methane, a powerful greenhouse gas. Methane makes up slightly more than half of all livestock emissions5. Cattle also grow slowly, so each animal eats and emits for a long time before it is slaughtered.
Per kilogram, the gap is enormous. A kilogram of beef from a beef herd comes with around 99 kilograms of greenhouse gases, against about 10 for chicken6. Beef also needs about 15,400 cubic metres of water per tonne on average worldwide, mostly to grow the grass and feed, more than three times as much as chicken7.

## Pasture is the biggest driver of tropical deforestation
Cattle need space, and a lot of it comes from cleared forest. Between 2005 and 2013, the expansion of pasture for beef was responsible for 41% of all tropical deforestation, about 2.1 million hectares a year, more than any other single product. Beef production in Brazil alone accounted for about a quarter of all tropical forest lost8.
In the Amazon, the pattern is familiar: forest is cleared and turned into cattle pasture. Soy, palm oil and other crops play their part too, but beef is the largest single driver8.
The forests being cut down or burned, much of it for cattle pasture.

## Where beef is heading
Beef is growing more slowly than other meats. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and FAO expect beef consumption to rise by about 13% by 2034, while poultry grows by about 21%9. As a result, the livestock sector’s emissions are projected to rise by only about 6%, half as fast as meat production, because a growing share of the world’s meat comes from chicken rather than beef9.
That is good news for the climate, and bad news for the animal count: replacing the meat from one cow takes about 210 chickens, which is why the number of animals slaughtered keeps climbing much faster than the number of cattle. The full story is on the page for chickens slaughtered for meat.
The biggest question for cattle may be the Amazon. If Brazil manages to protect its forests while its cattle industry grows, it will show that beef and forests can coexist. If pasture keeps pushing into the rainforest, the true cost of a burger will keep including a piece of the world’s largest tropical forest. Which way it goes will depend far more on laws and their enforcement than on how much beef any one person eats.
Every land animal slaughtered for meat this year, cattle included.
Last updated 23 September 2026
How this number was made▾
This is the number of cattle FAO recorded as slaughtered for meat in 2024, the latest year published, spread evenly across the current year, so it runs at the 2024 pace. It includes dairy cows slaughtered at the end of their milking lives as well as cattle raised for beef. Buffalo are counted separately. The number grew only about 0.6% a year over the last decade, so we do not project it forward.
*    304,744,672 cattle slaughtered per year
FAO's measured 2024 total. Not extrapolated, since the series grows only about 0.6% a year and a projection would change the figure by little more than rounding.

In this resource, updated with the latest available data, we aggregate and explore trends in animal slaughter around the world using UN FAO data tracked since 1960.

# Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts
#### Latest Update: April 2026
Next Scheduled Update: April 2027
Welcome to the Faunalytics Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts hub.
In this comprehensive resource, we look at the number of animals slaughtered globally for food every year, based on data gathered by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).

# Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts
### Source
The data for land animals comes fromthe FAOSTAT database, obtained using the following filters: “Producing Animals/Slaughtered” in “Elements” and by selecting the relevant animals in “Livestock primary > (List)” under “Items.”
The data for fishes was pulled from the FishStatJ database, the software for fisheries and aquaculture from the FAO. You can retrieve the data from “Global Production By Production Source 1950-2024,” the most recent dataset, using the following filters: “Fish and other fishing products” under “CPC Division” and both “Aquaculture production” and “Capture production” under “Production Source.” The FAOSTAT database counts land animals by the individual animal slaughtered, but this is not the case for fishes, who are measured in live weight (units are either tons or kilograms).
The human population data used to calculate per capita numbers comes from the UN FAO database. You can retrieve the data by filtering for “Total Population – Both Sexes” in “Elements.” This database is updated biannually, so for years when updated population numbers are not released, we use projections based on the “Year Projections” filter.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
Every day, more than 230 million land animals are slaughtered for meat worldwide. Nine in ten are chickens.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026. The figure comes from the FAO, the United Nations food and agriculture agency. Yet it leaves out most of the animals killed: fish. Nobody counts them one by one, but a study published in 2024 estimates that fishing catches between 3 and 6 billion of them a day.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6. This article traces each figure back to its source, then looks at what a donation can change.
In brief
*   In 2024, **86 billion** land animals were slaughtered for meat worldwide, roughly **2,700 a second**.  
*   Farmed fish are killed in the **hundreds of billions** each year, and wild fish in the **trillions**.  
*   In France, around **2.6 million** land animals are sent to slaughter every day.  
*   Your donations can prevent a great deal of animal suffering: by our estimates, **€0.85** spares one hen a life in a cage, on average.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Per day, per year, per second
Every year, the FAO publishes the number of animals slaughtered for meat in each country. Our World in Data compiles these figures and makes them available to download. In 2024, the most recent year available, the total reached 86.3 billion animals across seven species: chickens, ducks, pigs, sheep, goats, turkeys and cattle.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026.
That works out at 236 million animals a day, or 2,700 a second.
This total is a minimum: rabbits, geese, guinea fowl and horses are not included.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Species by species
Chickens Other species
Land animals slaughtered per day worldwide in 2024. Linear scale: next to the chickens, the bars for the other species are barely visible. Source: FAO, via Our World in Data.
| Species | Slaughtered in 2024 | Per day (approx.) | Share of total |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Chickens | 78.5 billion | 215 million | 91% |  
| Ducks | 4.2 billion | 11.6 million | 4.9% |  
| Pigs | 1.5 billion | 4.1 million | 1.7% |  
| Sheep | 704 million | 1.9 million | 0.8% |  
| Goats | 564 million | 1.5 million | 0.7% |  
| Turkeys | 504 million | 1.4 million | 0.6% |  
| Cattle | 305 million | 830,000 | 0.4% |  
| Total | 86.3 billion | 236 million | 100% |
Source: FAO, via Our World in Data. Per day: annual total divided by 365.25.
Worldwide, around 257 chickens are slaughtered for every head of cattle.
The lives of these animals can change. A single campaign aimed at companies can affect millions of them: in 2023, The Humane League pressed 62 companies to honour their own commitments, which cover 42 million hens. We come back to this at the end of the article.

## Why chickens make up 9 in 10 of the animals slaughtered
Weight explains much of the gap. In France, a broiler chicken yields 1.6 kg of meat on average (carcass weight), compared with 323 kg for one head of cattle.[[3]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn3)Agreste (2025). Statistique agricole annuelle 2024, résultats définitifs (French annual agricultural statistics). Chiffres et données no. 16, pp. 2... It therefore takes around 200 chickens to produce as much meat as a single cow or bull.
Slaughter age matters too. In the European Union, a fast-growing chicken goes to slaughter at around 37 days old, weighing 2 to 2.5 kg, before it has even reached sexual maturity. According to EFSA, the European Food Safety Authority, this is the result of genetic selection: between 1950 and 2000, the growth rate of these chickens quadrupled.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126. Slower-growing breeds, such as Label Rouge chickens, must reach at least 70 to 81 days before slaughter.
This intensive model supplies 90% of broiler chickens in the European Union. The animals bear the cost: EFSA reports walking problems of genetic origin in these birds, which breeders have reduced but never eliminated.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126.

## What about fish?
The FAO counts fish in tonnes, never as individuals.[[5]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn5)Roser, M. (2023). How many animals get slaughtered every day? Our World in Data. To work out how many there are, you have to divide the tonnage by an average weight for each species. Alison Mood and Phil Brooke (fishcount) did exactly that in two studies published in the scientific journal _Animal Welfare_.
236 m land animals slaughtered per day (2024)
340 m farmed fish killed per day (central estimate, 2019)
3 to 6 bn wild fish caught per day (2000-2019 average)

## What about fish?
### Farmed fish
In 2019, between 78 and 171 billion farmed fish were killed for food. The central estimate is 124 billion, or around 340 million a day. According to the authors, farmed fish now outnumber all the farmed birds and mammals slaughtered. Their number has risen ninefold since 1990.[[6]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn6)Mood, A., Lara, E., Boyland, N. K. and Brooke, P. (2023). Estimating global numbers of farmed fishes killed for food annually from 1990 to 2019. An...

## What about fish?
### Wild fish
Fishing kills even more. Between 2000 and 2019, an average of 1.1 to 2.2 trillion wild fish were caught each year, or 3 to 6 billion a day. According to the authors, more than half of them are turned into fishmeal and fish oil.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6.

## What can we do about these figures?
More than 99% of the animals killed for human consumption are farmed animals. Yet in the United States, only 3% of donations to animal charities go to farmed animals, while companion animals receive 95%.[[10]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn10)Animal Charity Evaluators (2025). Why Farmed Animals?
A cause this underfunded often leaves proven work without resources, and a donation goes further there. The Humane League, for example, negotiates with companies to stop buying eggs from caged hens. Based on the results of its campaigns, we estimate that a donation of €0.85 spares one hen a life in a cage, on average. This is an average: the real impact varies from one campaign to the next, and not every company keeps its commitments on time.
Other charities focus on the most numerous animals. The Shrimp Welfare Project provides electrical stunners to shrimp producers, so that the animals are unconscious when they are slaughtered.[[11]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn11)Shrimp Welfare Project. Humane Slaughter Initiative. We present these charities on our Animal welfare page.

How many animals are killed every second worldwide?  
Around 2,700 land animals a second in 2024, according to FAO data. Including fish, the real figure is far higher, but too uncertain to give per second.
Which animal is slaughtered most in the world?  
Among land animals, the chicken: 78.5 billion in 2024, or 91% of the total. If fish are included, wild fish come first, with 1.1 to 2.2 trillion caught each year.
How many chickens are killed every day worldwide?  
Around 215 million a day in 2024, or nearly 150,000 a minute.
How many animals are slaughtered each year in France?  
Around 943 million land animals in 2024, including 735 million chickens.
How many fish are killed each year worldwide?  
The most recent estimates put the figure at 78 to 171 billion farmed fish killed in 2019, and 1.1 to 2.2 trillion wild fish caught each year on average between 2000 and 2019. The FAO only counts fish in tonnes, which explains these wide ranges.

Yes. The world slaughtered 7.9 billion land animals in 1961, compared with 86.3 billion in 2024, eleven times as many. The number of farmed fish killed has risen ninefold since 1990.

According to Faunalytics, 7.8 billion male chicks were killed worldwide in the egg industry in 2024. They do not appear in the FAO's slaughter figures.
How can I help farmed animals with a donation?  
By supporting the charities whose impact is best documented. The Humane League, for example, persuades companies to stop using eggs from caged hens: we estimate that a donation of €0.85 spares one hen a life in a cage, on average. You will find our recommendations on our list of effective animal welfare charities.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
Every day, more than 230 million land animals are slaughtered for meat worldwide. Nine in ten are chickens.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026. The figure comes from the FAO, the United Nations food and agriculture agency. Yet it leaves out most of the animals killed: fish. Nobody counts them one by one, but a study published in 2024 estimates that fishing catches between 3 and 6 billion of them a day.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6. This article traces each figure back to its source, then looks at what a donation can change.
In brief
*   In 2024, **86 billion** land animals were slaughtered for meat worldwide, roughly **2,700 a second**.  
*   Farmed fish are killed in the **hundreds of billions** each year, and wild fish in the **trillions**.  
*   In France, around **2.6 million** land animals are sent to slaughter every day.  
*   Your donations can prevent a great deal of animal suffering: by our estimates, **€0.85** spares one hen a life in a cage, on average.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Per day, per year, per second
Every year, the FAO publishes the number of animals slaughtered for meat in each country. Our World in Data compiles these figures and makes them available to download. That works out at 236 million animals a day, or 2,700 a second.
This total is a minimum: rabbits, geese, guinea fowl and horses are not included.

# Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts
#### Latest Update: April 2026
Next Scheduled Update: April 2027
Welcome to the Faunalytics Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts hub.
In this comprehensive resource, we look at the number of animals slaughtered globally for food every year, based on data gathered by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).
texts.6:
# Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts
### Source
The data for land animals comes fromthe FAOSTAT database, obtained using the following filters: “Producing Animals/Slaughtered” in “Elements” and by selecting the relevant animals in “Livestock primary > (List)” under “Items.”
The data for fishes was pulled from the FishStatJ database, the software for fisheries and aquaculture from the FAO. You can retrieve the data from “Global Production By Production Source 1950-2024,” the most recent dataset, using the following filters: “Fish and other fishing products” under “CPC Division” and both “Aquaculture production” and “Capture production” under “Production Source.” The FAOSTAT database counts land animals by the individual animal slaughtered, but this is not the case for fishes, who are measured in live weight (units are either tons or kilograms).
The human population data used to calculate per capita numbers comes from the UN FAO database. You can retrieve the data by filtering for “Total Population – Both Sexes” in “Elements.” This database is updated biannually, so for years when updated population numbers are not released, we use projections based on the “Year Projections” filter.

Title: How many animals are slaughtered every day worldwide?
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,13,14,15,16
Animal welfare

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
Every day, more than 230 million land animals are slaughtered for meat worldwide. Nine in ten are chickens.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026. The figure comes from the FAO, the United Nations food and agriculture agency. Yet it leaves out most of the animals killed: fish. Nobody counts them one by one, but a study published in 2024 estimates that fishing catches between 3 and 6 billion of them a day.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6. This article traces each figure back to its source, then looks at what a donation can change.
In brief
*   In 2024, **86 billion** land animals were slaughtered for meat worldwide, roughly **2,700 a second**.  
*   Farmed fish are killed in the **hundreds of billions** each year, and wild fish in the **trillions**.  
*   In France, around **2.6 million** land animals are sent to slaughter every day.  
*   Your donations can prevent a great deal of animal suffering: by our estimates, **€0.85** spares one hen a life in a cage, on average.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Per day, per year, per second
Every year, the FAO publishes the number of animals slaughtered for meat in each country. Our World in Data compiles these figures and makes them available to download. In 2024, the most recent year available, the total reached 86.3 billion animals across seven species: chickens, ducks, pigs, sheep, goats, turkeys and cattle.[[1]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn1)Our World in Data (2026). Yearly number of animals slaughtered for meat. FAO data, downloaded on 27/10/2026.
That works out at 236 million animals a day, or 2,700 a second.
This total is a minimum: rabbits, geese, guinea fowl and horses are not included.

## How many animals are slaughtered every day? The figures by species
### Species by species
Chickens Other species
Land animals slaughtered per day worldwide in 2024. Linear scale: next to the chickens, the bars for the other species are barely visible. Source: FAO, via Our World in Data.
| Species | Slaughtered in 2024 | Per day (approx.) | Share of total |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Chickens | 78.5 billion | 215 million | 91% |  
| Ducks | 4.2 billion | 11.6 million | 4.9% |  
| Pigs | 1.5 billion | 4.1 million | 1.7% |  
| Sheep | 704 million | 1.9 million | 0.8% |  
| Goats | 564 million | 1.5 million | 0.7% |  
| Turkeys | 504 million | 1.4 million | 0.6% |  
| Cattle | 305 million | 830,000 | 0.4% |  
| Total | 86.3 billion | 236 million | 100% |
Source: FAO, via Our World in Data. Per day: annual total divided by 365.25.
Worldwide, around 257 chickens are slaughtered for every head of cattle.
The lives of these animals can change. A single campaign aimed at companies can affect millions of them: in 2023, The Humane League pressed 62 companies to honour their own commitments, which cover 42 million hens. We come back to this at the end of the article.

## Why chickens make up 9 in 10 of the animals slaughtered
Weight explains much of the gap. In France, a broiler chicken yields 1.6 kg of meat on average (carcass weight), compared with 323 kg for one head of cattle.[[3]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn3)Agreste (2025). Statistique agricole annuelle 2024, résultats définitifs (French annual agricultural statistics). Chiffres et données no. 16, pp. 2... It therefore takes around 200 chickens to produce as much meat as a single cow or bull.
Slaughter age matters too. In the European Union, a fast-growing chicken goes to slaughter at around 37 days old, weighing 2 to 2.5 kg, before it has even reached sexual maturity. According to EFSA, the European Food Safety Authority, this is the result of genetic selection: between 1950 and 2000, the growth rate of these chickens quadrupled.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126. Slower-growing breeds, such as Label Rouge chickens, must reach at least 70 to 81 days before slaughter.
This intensive model supplies 90% of broiler chickens in the European Union. The animals bear the cost: EFSA reports walking problems of genetic origin in these birds, which breeders have reduced but never eliminated.[[4]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn4)EFSA Panel on Animal Health and Animal Welfare (2023). Welfare of broilers on farm. EFSA Journal, 21(2), 7788, pp. 3, 23 and 126.

## What about fish?
The FAO counts fish in tonnes, never as individuals.[[5]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn5)Roser, M. (2023). How many animals get slaughtered every day? Our World in Data. To work out how many there are, you have to divide the tonnage by an average weight for each species. Alison Mood and Phil Brooke (fishcount) did exactly that in two studies published in the scientific journal _Animal Welfare_.
236 m land animals slaughtered per day (2024)
340 m farmed fish killed per day (central estimate, 2019)
3 to 6 bn wild fish caught per day (2000-2019 average)

## What about fish?
### Farmed fish
In 2019, between 78 and 171 billion farmed fish were killed for food. The central estimate is 124 billion, or around 340 million a day. According to the authors, farmed fish now outnumber all the farmed birds and mammals slaughtered. Their number has risen ninefold since 1990.[[6]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn6)Mood, A., Lara, E., Boyland, N. K. and Brooke, P. (2023). Estimating global numbers of farmed fishes killed for food annually from 1990 to 2019. An...

## What about fish?
### Wild fish
Fishing kills even more. Between 2000 and 2019, an average of 1.1 to 2.2 trillion wild fish were caught each year, or 3 to 6 billion a day. According to the authors, more than half of them are turned into fishmeal and fish oil.[[2]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn2)Mood, A. and Brooke, P. (2024). Estimating global numbers of fishes caught from the wild annually from 2000 to 2019. Animal Welfare, 33, e6.

## What can we do about these figures?
More than 99% of the animals killed for human consumption are farmed animals. Yet in the United States, only 3% of donations to animal charities go to farmed animals, while companion animals receive 95%.[[10]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn10)Animal Charity Evaluators (2025). Why Farmed Animals?
A cause this underfunded often leaves proven work without resources, and a donation goes further there. The Humane League, for example, negotiates with companies to stop buying eggs from caged hens. Based on the results of its campaigns, we estimate that a donation of €0.85 spares one hen a life in a cage, on average. This is an average: the real impact varies from one campaign to the next, and not every company keeps its commitments on time.
Other charities focus on the most numerous animals. The Shrimp Welfare Project provides electrical stunners to shrimp producers, so that the animals are unconscious when they are slaughtered.[[11]](https://mieuxdonner.org/how-many-animals-slaughtered-every-day/#fn11)Shrimp Welfare Project. Humane Slaughter Initiative. We present these charities on our Animal welfare page.
While you were reading
Around 2,700 land animals are slaughtered every second worldwide.
Estimate: 86.3 billion animals in 2024, spread evenly across the year (FAO).

## Frequently asked questions
How many animals are killed every second worldwide?  
Around 2,700 land animals a second in 2024, according to FAO data. Including fish, the real figure is far higher, but too uncertain to give per second.
Which animal is slaughtered most in the world?  
Among land animals, the chicken: 78.5 billion in 2024, or 91% of the total. If fish are included, wild fish come first, with 1.1 to 2.2 trillion caught each year.
How many chickens are killed every day worldwide?  
Around 215 million a day in 2024, or nearly 150,000 a minute.
How many animals are slaughtered each year in France?  
Around 943 million land animals in 2024, including 735 million chickens.
How many fish are killed each year worldwide?  
The most recent estimates put the figure at 78 to 171 billion farmed fish killed in 2019, and 1.1 to 2.2 trillion wild fish caught each year on average between 2000 and 2019. The FAO only counts fish in tonnes, which explains these wide ranges.
Is the number of animals slaughtered rising?  
Yes. The world slaughtered 7.9 billion land animals in 1961, compared with 86.3 billion in 2024, eleven times as many. The number of farmed fish killed has risen ninefold since 1990.
How many male chicks are killed each year?  
According to Faunalytics, 7.8 billion male chicks were killed worldwide in the egg industry in 2024. They do not appear in the FAO's slaughter figures.
How can I help farmed animals with a donation?  
By supporting the charities whose impact is best documented. The Humane League, for example, persuades companies to stop using eggs from caged hens: we estimate that a donation of €0.85 spares one hen a life in a cage, on average. You will find our recommendations on our list of effective animal welfare charities.

# Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts
#### Latest Update: April 2026
Next Scheduled Update: April 2027
Welcome to the Faunalytics Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts hub.
In this comprehensive resource, we look at the number of animals slaughtered globally for food every year, based on data gathered by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).

# Global Animal Slaughter Statistics & Charts
### Source
The data for land animals comes fromthe FAOSTAT database, obtained using the following filters: “Producing Animals/Slaughtered” in “Elements” and by selecting the relevant animals in “Livestock primary > (List)” under “Items.”
The data for fishes was pulled from the FishStatJ database, the software for fisheries and aquaculture from the FAO. You can retrieve the data from “Global Production By Production Source 1950-2024,” the most recent dataset, using the following filters: “Fish and other fishing products” under “CPC Division” and both “Aquaculture production” and “Capture production” under “Production Source.” The FAOSTAT database counts land animals by the individual animal slaughtered, but this is not the case for fishes, who are measured in live weight (units are either tons or kilograms).
The human population data used to calculate per capita numbers comes from the UN FAO database. You can retrieve the data by filtering for “Total Population – Both Sexes” in “Elements.” This database is updated biannually, so for years when updated population numbers are not released, we use projections based on the “Year Projections” filter.
